entries.title: Active Theory · Creative Digital Experiences
entries.why: A strong reference for turning a studio homepage into one immersive stage: the shell is built around a full-viewport scene, sparse copy, custom typography, and deliberate loader-to-experience boot behavior.

entries.title: Resn - Creative Digital Agency
entries.why: A compact reference for the older but still useful immersive-agency shell: black-screen loader, progress bar, JS bootstrapping, and a positioning stack that explicitly spans motion, audio, 3D, and interactive graphics.
entries.implementationFormat: black-background loader shell with RequireJS runtime boot

entries.title: Cuberto | We create digital solutions
entries.why: A high-signal motion reference that keeps its craft in the DOM: custom cursor inversion, animated loader, menu overlay, reel sections, postcard flips, CTA ripples, and repeated autoplay media all work together as one branded interaction system.
entries.implementationFormat: HTML-first scroll experience with custom cursor, video loops, and overlay navigation

entries.title: KODE Immersive - Tech-Enabled Creativity, Unforgettable Experiences.
entries.format: Nuxt-based immersive agency homepage with canvas scenes and guided interaction
entries.why: A strong reference for blending cinematic staging with explicit interaction prompts: the site treats the preloader, scratch reveal, step-based services section, and sound controls as one continuous narrative system instead of separate gimmicks.
entries.implementationFormat: Nuxt-rendered immersive scroll site with persistent canvases, overlay UI, and step-based chapter controls

entries.title: Year in Review 2025 - Unseen Studio
entries.format: horizontal editorial timeline with video chapters and parallax text
entries.why: A high-signal reference for turning a studio recap into an immersive editorial object: the experience uses a horizontal scroll container, a giant dashed timeline, looping media, month-based chaptering, and outbound case-study links without losing its narrative cohesion.
entries.implementationFormat: WordPress-driven horizontal timeline with SVG rail, canvas intro stage, and looping chapter media

entries.title: Experience & advantages - David Whyte
entries.format: immersive companion-portal introduction with canvas, audio loops, and map-driven wayfinding
entries.why: A distinctive reference for bringing editorial, audio, and membership-product storytelling into one immersive entry flow: the page uses watercolor-style stage media, sound controls, a scroll-to-explore prompt, and map-backed navigation to make a content archive feel like an explorable world.
entries.implementationFormat: WordPress experience page with custom loader, canvas stage, audio loops, and map-backed portal navigation

compositions.title: Single viewport scene shell
compositions.study: The page is organized around one `#Stage` container that claims the full viewport instead of behaving like a normal document scroll.
compositions.reuse: Use when a motion-led site should feel like entering one scene rather than browsing stacked sections.

compositions.title: Loader before scene boot
compositions.study: The HTML boot path preloads the main app script and treats the scene as a runtime that must be ready before the experience starts.
compositions.reuse: Use when cinematic pacing matters more than instant content dump, but keep fallback messaging visible.

compositions.title: Progress bar landing shell
compositions.study: The first visible layer is a full-screen loader with a dedicated progress bar before the runtime is attached.
compositions.reuse: Use when the experience benefits from a deliberate prelude instead of jumping straight into content.

compositions.title: Black-canvas base layer
compositions.study: The shell sets a black background and defers the interactive experience to a JS loader rather than laying out a normal DOM-first homepage.
compositions.reuse: Use for immersive portfolios or studio sites where motion direction should own the first impression.

compositions.title: Brand and capability reels
compositions.study: Repeated reel sections turn logos, services, and social links into kinetic strips rather than static logo farms.
compositions.reuse: Use when repeated content should feel alive without becoming decorative noise.

compositions.title: Postcard service stack
compositions.study: Service content is structured as front/back postcard cards so motion can reveal more depth without leaving the page.
compositions.reuse: Use when hover or tap should expose a second information layer inside the same section.

compositions.title: Typographic loader overlay
compositions.study: The loader is treated as a branded scene with oversized typography instead of a generic spinner.
compositions.reuse: Make wait states part of the visual system when the site sells craft.

compositions.entryTitle: KODE Immersive - Tech-Enabled Creativity, Unforgettable Experiences.
compositions.title: Enter-gated preloader scene
compositions.study: The first frame is a branded preloader with a hidden counter, lottie animation, and an explicit Enter action instead of an automatic handoff.
compositions.reuse: Use when a story-led site should give visitors a moment to opt into the experience instead of dropping them straight into the main scroll.

compositions.entryTitle: KODE Immersive - Tech-Enabled Creativity, Unforgettable Experiences.
compositions.title: Alternating text and canvas chapters
compositions.study: The page alternates oversized justified text panels, fixed bottom-bar cues, canvas-backed scenes, and narrative copy blocks to keep the scroll rhythm varied.
compositions.reuse: Use when immersive storytelling needs strong pacing changes between copy-heavy beats and visual interaction beats.

compositions.entryTitle: KODE Immersive - Tech-Enabled Creativity, Unforgettable Experiences.
compositions.title: Full-viewport canvas shell
compositions.study: Canvas layers for the background, mouse trails, chevrons, noise, and hero moments stay mounted around the content instead of appearing as one isolated hero widget.
compositions.reuse: Keep the stage infrastructure persistent when motion cues should connect the whole page rather than one section.

compositions.title: 32,000px timeline spine
compositions.study: The story rides on one oversized SVG line that behaves like a visual rail through the entire year.
compositions.reuse: Use when a long-form motion story needs one persistent orienting device instead of restarting the layout each chapter.

compositions.title: Month-by-month horizontal chapters
compositions.study: Each month is framed as its own chapter with date typography, short editorial copy, and a dedicated media beat.
compositions.reuse: Use for portfolios, annual reports, or product histories that benefit from clearly named sequential beats.

compositions.title: Intro stage with canvas and looped eye video
compositions.study: The introduction combines fixed overlay typography, a canvas layer, and a hidden autoplay eye-loop video before the month timeline begins.
compositions.reuse: Open long-form stories with one theatrical stage that teaches the interaction model before the dense content starts.

compositions.title: Dedicated experience loader
compositions.study: The page has a specific LoaderExperience component before the exploratory stage begins, which separates the portal from the surrounding marketing site.
compositions.reuse: Use a dedicated loader when a special-mode experience should feel distinct from the rest of the site.

compositions.title: Canvas-led portal shell
compositions.study: A shared canvas, hidden video textures, audio loops, and stage controls frame the portal as one continuous environment rather than a collection of article cards.
compositions.reuse: Treat media, sound, and navigation as one shell when the goal is to create a world instead of a page.

compositions.title: Exploration steps into portal features
compositions.study: The experience introduces archive, map, poetry, and membership benefits as staged reveals with their own copy and CTA layers.
compositions.reuse: Use progressive feature reveals when a content-heavy platform would feel too abstract as a static benefits list.

assets.notes: The shell loads multiple weights of NB Architekt before the main app boot sequence.
assets.reuse: Treat typography as part of the stage system, not a last-minute decorative layer.

assets.notes: The viewport is reserved for a JS-driven stage rather than a static hero image.
assets.reuse: Plan scene ownership, boot timing, and mobile fallbacks before building visual motion.

assets.notes: The page metadata and shell language point to a media system that mixes video with interactive graphics.
assets.reuse: Plan media as a native part of the experience instead of one disconnected hero clip.

assets.notes: Progress bars and browser-support messaging are treated as first-class visual layers.
assets.reuse: Keep boot, wait, and failure states visually aligned with the main stage.

assets.notes: The page uses many autoplay, muted video loops across achievements, icon moments, and footer background.
assets.reuse: Break video into small narrative loops instead of relying on one massive hero clip.

assets.notes: Matter and Gallery Modern create contrast between operational copy and expressive headlines.
assets.reuse: Use two-role typography systems when motion design needs both clarity and theater.

assets.role: card fronts, reels, and footer stage
assets.notes: Images and video are attached to multiple modules rather than isolated in one showcase section.
assets.reuse: Distribute media across the scroll so every chapter has its own movement vocabulary.

assets.entryTitle: KODE Immersive - Tech-Enabled Creativity, Unforgettable Experiences.
assets.notes: The homepage reserves multiple canvases for the preloader, background, chevron, noise, and scratch interactions.
assets.reuse: Plan canvas ownership at the page shell level when multiple chapters depend on the same motion runtime.

assets.entryTitle: KODE Immersive - Tech-Enabled Creativity, Unforgettable Experiences.
assets.role: voice contrast between operational copy and expressive display
assets.notes: Aeonik Pro and OT Brut separate practical labels from oversized theatrical headlines.
assets.reuse: Use a two-role type system when interaction prompts need to feel exact but the headline voice still needs drama.

assets.entryTitle: KODE Immersive - Tech-Enabled Creativity, Unforgettable Experiences.
assets.role: preloader, bottom bars, and contact overlay controls
assets.notes: The site treats entry, scroll cues, sound toggles, and contact information as styled overlays rather than generic utility chrome.
assets.reuse: Make utility states part of the same visual world as the immersive content.

assets.role: chapter media and intro stage texture
assets.notes: The intro uses an autoplay loop and many chapters rely on looping MP4 moments instead of static thumbnails.
assets.reuse: Use short loops to keep long editorial stories visually alive without requiring full video playback controls in every panel.

assets.notes: The experience mixes mono labels, heavy condensed numerals, and script accents to make dates feel collectible rather than administrative.
assets.reuse: Treat temporal labels as a design system of their own when the story structure depends on time.

assets.role: chapter images, loops, and linked case-study references
assets.notes: Individual chapters pair media with short text and, in some cases, direct Open links to deeper case pages.
assets.reuse: Let each chapter decide whether it needs a passive media note or a link-out to a deeper artifact.

assets.notes: The page preloads base and over video textures for the experience stage rather than relying on one visible hero clip.
assets.reuse: Layer quiet texture channels behind a canvas stage when the atmosphere matters as much as the content.

assets.role: loader, scroll cue, and sound controls
assets.notes: Loader, scroll prompt, and sound state are surfaced as explicit stage overlays, not hidden implementation details.
assets.reuse: Make media controls visible when sound and pacing are core to the story.

assets.role: portal feature reveals across archive, maps, and membership
assets.notes: The experience combines portal copy, CTAs, audio, and supporting visuals to present multiple content surfaces inside one guided journey.
assets.reuse: Bundle feature explanation with sensory cues when a platform's value is experiential rather than purely functional.

motion.title: Boot into stage
motion.notes: The shell prioritizes an app preload and transitions into the runtime scene instead of rendering a static homepage first.
motion.fallback: When JS is unavailable, the page only exposes a direct enable-JS message, so this entry needs a later fallback review.

motion.title: Scene-led chaptering
motion.notes: The static shell hints at a stage that owns the viewport and likely swaps chapters inside one continuous scene.
motion.fallback: Not verified live; backfill with a browser pass before reusing the chapter model directly.

motion.title: Progress-led boot sequence
motion.notes: The shell exposes `loader__` elements plus a foreground progress bar to pace entry into the experience.
motion.fallback: Old-browser messaging exists, but reduced-motion behavior was not visible from static inspection.

motion.title: Runtime-owned motion narrative
motion.notes: Because RequireJS loads the actual experience, the motion system likely owns its own chaptering rather than relying on default document scroll.
motion.fallback: Needs live browser review before treating the exact chapter model as reusable guidance.

motion.title: Word-by-word loader reveal
motion.notes: The loader overlay uses oversized words, percent progress, and fill transitions to pace entry into the site.
motion.fallback: Reduced-motion handling was not verified, so keep this as inspiration-only until a live follow-up confirms it.

motion.title: Full-screen menu transition
motion.notes: Navigation expands into a fixed overlay instead of acting like a simple dropdown or topbar.
motion.fallback: When motion is reduced, the overlay should still preserve direct access to every destination.

motion.title: Micro-looped media throughout the scroll
motion.notes: Video loops are embedded in multiple sections so motion energy stays distributed instead of front-loaded.
motion.fallback: Each loop should degrade to a clear poster frame or still image.

motion.title: Cursor polarity shifts
motion.notes: Multiple sections switch to an inverse cursor mode to turn the pointer into part of the visual language.
motion.fallback: Pointer styling should remain optional for touch devices and non-pointer environments.

motion.entryTitle: KODE Immersive - Tech-Enabled Creativity, Unforgettable Experiences.
motion.title: Manual entry into the experience
motion.notes: A lottie-led preloader and Enter button pace the first transition into the scroll instead of starting automatically.
motion.fallback: Reduced-motion handling was not verified; keep the entry gate optional and preserve direct access to the main content when reusing the pattern.

motion.entryTitle: KODE Immersive - Tech-Enabled Creativity, Unforgettable Experiences.
motion.title: Persistent scroll cue choreography
motion.notes: Fixed bottom bars repeatedly restate Scroll for more so the story keeps a guided tempo even as the visual treatment flips between white and black modes.
motion.fallback: Scroll cues should not be the only instruction path on touch or keyboard-driven browsing.

motion.entryTitle: KODE Immersive - Tech-Enabled Creativity, Unforgettable Experiences.
motion.title: Canvas-backed micro-scenes
motion.notes: The site layers moving canvas scenes and animated text transitions across several sections rather than concentrating all movement in the hero.
motion.fallback: Provide still or low-motion equivalents for every chapter so the narrative can survive without animated canvas effects.

motion.title: Horizontal scroll narrative
motion.notes: The main container switches the default reading direction into a horizontal timeline that feels closer to a moving exhibition wall than a normal webpage.
motion.fallback: Reduced-motion and keyboard handling were not verified live, so reuse this pattern only when an alternate navigation path is designed up front.

motion.title: Distributed chapter loops
motion.notes: Looping video is distributed across the intro and chapter bodies so motion remains present throughout the full recap.
motion.fallback: Each loop should degrade to a readable still frame when autoplay is unavailable.

motion.title: Intro-led onboarding into the timeline
motion.notes: The opening title card, scroll instruction, and hidden webgl stage teach the experience before the dense story begins.
motion.fallback: If the animated intro is skipped, preserve the year title and scroll instruction in plain text.

motion.title: Portal boot before exploration
motion.notes: The experience isolates its own loader and then hands off into a dedicated scroll-to-explore stage.
motion.fallback: Keep the portal discoverable through a plain content path if the animated stage cannot boot.

motion.title: Guided exploration through portal benefits
motion.notes: A Scroll to explore control introduces a staged journey through library, map, and membership features instead of a static landing page.
motion.fallback: Exploration prompts should degrade to visible section links or buttons when animation is reduced.

motion.title: Ambient media plus looped soundscape
motion.notes: The experience coordinates hidden video textures with several looped audio tracks to create atmosphere around the portal.
motion.fallback: Sound must remain opt-in and the story should still read without autoplay media.

interactions.title: Pointer-safe scene container
interactions.study: The shell disables user selection, suppresses default touch behavior, and routes interaction through the stage container.
interactions.reuse: Use when the pointer should manipulate or explore the scene instead of selecting the page.

interactions.title: Runtime-owned interaction model
interactions.study: The page is architected as a JS application with its own unsupported-browser branch and iOS/mobile handling.
interactions.reuse: Treat device branches and capability checks as part of the interaction design, not only engineering cleanup.

interactions.title: Boot-gated interaction model
interactions.study: The interactive experience is explicitly gated behind the runtime loader instead of exposing plain content immediately.
interactions.reuse: Use when navigation and interaction should feel like part of one audiovisual world.

interactions.title: Capability-checked stage entry
interactions.study: The shell ships a compatibility branch for old browsers and then hands off to JS, which makes capability checks part of the interaction contract.
interactions.reuse: Treat capability gates as a visible part of immersive design rather than a silent crash path.

interactions.title: Inverse cursor zones
interactions.study: Sections explicitly declare inverse cursor behavior, so the pointer acts like a scene element rather than a neutral browser arrow.
interactions.reuse: Use cursor styling sparingly to mark interaction mode shifts, not every hover target.

interactions.title: Cinematic navigation drawer
interactions.study: The nav toggle opens a full-screen menu with its own layout and reveal rhythm.
interactions.reuse: Use when the menu should feel like entering another chapter instead of covering the page with a utility tray.

interactions.title: Postcard front/back reveal
interactions.study: Cards present a media front and a text-heavy back, which makes hover or tap reveal part of the content structure.
interactions.reuse: Use for service grids where a single static card would either feel too shallow or too dense.

interactions.title: CTA ripple behavior
interactions.study: Buttons use border, ripple, and text-offset layers so basic calls to action inherit the same motion language as the rest of the site.
interactions.reuse: Make CTA motion consistent with the larger stage vocabulary instead of introducing one-off button effects.

interactions.entryTitle: KODE Immersive - Tech-Enabled Creativity, Unforgettable Experiences.
interactions.title: Scratch around logo reveal
interactions.study: A dedicated Scratch around prompt turns the logo canvas into an exploratory reveal instead of a passive brand mark.
interactions.reuse: Use when a reveal should feel playful and discoverable, but keep the hidden state non-essential.

interactions.entryTitle: KODE Immersive - Tech-Enabled Creativity, Unforgettable Experiences.
interactions.title: Prev/Next service navigator
interactions.study: The services section behaves like a numbered scene stepper with Prev and Next controls instead of a static accordion or grid.
interactions.reuse: Use for sequential service storytelling when each step needs its own canvas or animated state.

interactions.entryTitle: KODE Immersive - Tech-Enabled Creativity, Unforgettable Experiences.
interactions.title: Overlay-level sound control
interactions.study: The contact overlay includes a bracketed Sound On/Off control so audio state is treated as a first-class part of the experience.
interactions.reuse: Expose sound state explicitly whenever audio contributes to the brand experience.

interactions.title: This way onboarding cue
interactions.study: The intro explicitly tells the user that the story moves sideways, which prevents the horizontal layout from feeling like a bug.
interactions.reuse: Always teach a nonstandard scroll model with visible copy and directional affordances.

interactions.title: Chapter open links
interactions.study: Selected chapters provide Open buttons that branch into deeper work without breaking the year-in-review framing.
interactions.reuse: Use link-outs sparingly when a narrative summary needs optional deeper dives.

interactions.title: Parallax date and media choreography
interactions.study: Data-parallax attributes on years, images, and text turn the timeline into a layered motion field instead of a flat strip of cards.
interactions.reuse: Layer parallax sparingly to keep long-form storytelling tactile without overwhelming the reading flow.

interactions.title: Persistent sound state control
interactions.study: The stage exposes an explicit sound switch instead of assuming visitors want audio by default.
interactions.reuse: Use a persistent sound affordance whenever audio materially shapes the experience.

interactions.title: Map-backed literary navigation
interactions.study: Mapbox dependencies and copy about exploring literary landscapes position map navigation as a content surface, not a side utility.
interactions.reuse: Use when place is part of the story and the map should behave like narrative navigation rather than a locator widget.

interactions.title: Canvas-first exploration shell
interactions.study: The experience relies on a dedicated canvas, hidden media textures, and stage-layer controls to organize the interaction model.
interactions.reuse: Keep the interaction shell explicit when the page behaves more like an environment than a document.
